title: JT disk spectral preparation and ensemble boundaries

items.title: Adopted JT disk spectral model
items.physical_scope: An adopted continuous genus-zero disk density for the specified two-dimensional Jackiw–Teitelboim (JT) model in natural units. It asserts no particular individual exact energy spectrum, higher-topology contribution, or empirical validity.

items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=k_B=1$. Thus energy $E$ has units $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$, inverse temperature $\beta$ and the positive model parameter $C$ have units $\mathrm{s}$, and $S_0\in\mathbb R$ is dimensionless. In this item, **JT disk model** means only the disk-sector spectral model with the density specified below; the label refers to the cited two-dimensional Jackiw–Teitelboim calculations and adopts no additional field equation or path-integral construction. **Genus-zero disk contribution** means the single connected disk term, with one boundary and no handles, in the formal expansion by spacetime topology. A **nonperturbative completion** means additional exact model data that select an exact theory beyond the terms fixed by that formal expansion.

A **continuous spectral density** here is a nonnegative function $\rho_0:(0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ whose measure $\rho_0(E)\,dE$ assigns model spectral weight to energy intervals. Adopt

$$\rho_0(E):=e^{S_0}\frac{C}{2\pi^2}\sinh\!\left(2\pi\sqrt{2CE}\right),\qquad E>0.$$

The density has units $\mathrm{s}$, so $\rho_0(E)\,dE$ is dimensionless. This postulate specifies a continuous disk-level input only. It does not specify an individual discrete energy spectrum, sum higher-topology terms, choose a nonperturbative completion, or assert that the model describes nature.
items.design_state: Adopted the cited genus-zero disk density as a continuous model input, with natural-unit dimensions and explicit higher-topology and discrete-spectrum limits.

items.title: Exact disk-model Laplace integral and heat capacity
items.physical_scope: A conditional exact calculation for the adopted continuous genus-zero JT disk density, at fixed $C$ and $S_0$ in $c=\hbar=k_B=1$ units. It does not assert a discrete microscopic spectrum, a higher-topology result, a nonperturbative completion, or empirical validity.

references.title: Phil Saad, Stephen H. Shenker, and Douglas Stanford, JT gravity as a matrix integral, §§3.3.5 and 3.5
references.locator: SSS HTML §3.3.5, equation (125), gives the disk Schwarzian factor; §3.5, equations (143)–(144), give its Laplace-density relation and genus-zero density, not equation (145), which gives y(z). Set gamma=C and restore the separate exp(S_0) disk topological factor. The corresponding retrieved PDF equations are (122), printed p.30/PDF p.31, and (140)–(141), printed p.33/PDF p.34; topological weighting is equation (63), printed p.18/PDF p.19. The proof below evaluates the adopted Laplace integral locally.

references.title: Thomas G. Mertens and Gustavo J. Turiaci, Solvable models of quantum black holes: a review on Jackiw–Teitelboim gravity, §3.1
references.locator: Full-text review; equations (3.7) and (3.10) state the disk partition function and its continuous density in the same $C,S_0$ convention.

references.title: Gábor Sárosi, AdS2 holography and the SYK model, lecture notes, §3.3.1
references.locator: Full lecture notes; equations (54)–(55) give the Schwarzian disk thermal factor and thermodynamic relation. The local proof does not import their path-integral evaluation.

items.statement:
Let $C>0$ and $\beta>0$ have units of seconds, let $S_0\in\mathbb R$ be dimensionless, and use $c=\hbar=k_B=1$ units as in the adopted JT disk spectral model. Then $E>0$ has units $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ and the density $\rho_0(E)$ from that model has units seconds. Define the disk partition function as the Laplace integral

$$Z_0(\beta):=\int_0^\infty \rho_0(E)e^{-\beta E}\,dE.$$

When $Z_0(\beta)$ is finite and positive, define the normalized canonical energy distribution by $dP_\beta(E):=Z_0(\beta)^{-1}\rho_0(E)e^{-\beta E}\,dE$ and its mean energy by $\bar E(\beta):=\int_0^\infty E\,dP_\beta(E)$. Put $T:=1/\beta$ and, at fixed $C,S_0$, write $C_V/k_B:=d\bar E/dT$ for the dimensionless canonical heat-capacity coefficient in these units. Then the integral is finite and

$$Z_0(\beta)=e^{S_0}\frac{C\sqrt{2C}}{2\sqrt{\pi}\,\beta^{3/2}}\exp\!\left(\frac{2\pi^2C}{\beta}\right),\qquad \bar E(\beta)=\frac{3}{2\beta}+\frac{2\pi^2C}{\beta^2},\qquad \frac{C_V}{k_B}=\frac32+\frac{4\pi^2C}{\beta}>0.$$

These are deductions within the adopted continuous disk model, not claims about an individual microscopic spectrum or nature.
items.design_state: Proved the exact Laplace integral from the adopted density; added the published dominated-derivative supplier required by the Gaussian-cosh proof route.

title: JT disk spectral preparation and ensemble boundaries — Examples

items.title: The JT disk density does not determine a unique nonperturbative completion
items.physical_scope: A source-based limitation on interpreting the selected JT genus-zero disk density. It records that cited exact models extend beyond the single disk term and may average over theories; it makes no claim about every microscopic realization or nature.

references.title: Phil Saad, Stephen H. Shenker, and Douglas Stanford, JT gravity as a matrix integral, §§1 and 6
references.locator: Full-text article; §2.4 describes the double-scaling limit from ordinary matrix integrals; §§3.3.5 and 3.5 give the disk calculation, density and genus-expansion matching; §§1 and 6 discuss non-unique completion and the ensemble interpretation.

references.title: Thomas G. Mertens and Gustavo J. Turiaci, Solvable models of quantum black holes: a review on Jackiw–Teitelboim gravity, §§4.3.1–4.4 and 5.2
references.locator: Full-text review; §§4.3.1–4.4 discuss the SSS matrix-integral duality, density corrections, and nonperturbative limitations; §5.2 addresses factorization, discreteness, and ensemble averaging.

items.statement:
An **ensemble** here means the following finite-dimensional probability model. Let $N\ge 1$ be an integer, let $\mathcal H_N$ be an $N$-dimensional complex Hilbert space, and let $\operatorname{Herm}(\mathcal H_N)$ be the real vector space of self-adjoint linear operators on $\mathcal H_N$, with the operator-norm topology and its Borel sigma algebra. Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $\operatorname{Herm}(\mathcal H_N)$. Each $H\in\operatorname{Herm}(\mathcal H_N)$ is an energy operator, with units $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ in the natural units $c=\hbar=k_B=1$ of the adopted JT disk model. For inverse temperature $\beta>0$, with units seconds, define the finite-matrix partition function $Z_H(\beta):=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal H_N}(e^{-\beta H})$, where $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal H_N}$ is the ordinary finite-dimensional trace.

Since $H$ is self-adjoint and $\mathcal H_N$ is finite-dimensional, $Z_H(\beta)$ is a positive finite real number. The ensemble average is $\langle Z(\beta)\rangle_\mu:=\int_{\operatorname{Herm}(\mathcal H_N)}Z_H(\beta)\,d\mu(H)$; it is finite when $\int Z_H(\beta)\,d\mu(H)<\infty$.

A **nonperturbative completion** is additional exact model data that select an exact theory beyond the terms fixed by the formal expansion by spacetime topology, as in the adopted JT disk model. In the SSS construction, an ordinary ensemble of $L\times L$ Hermitian matrices has measure $d\mu_{L,a}(H)=\mathcal Z_{L,a}^{-1}e^{-L\operatorname{tr}V_{L,a}(H)}\,dH$ on $\operatorname{Herm}(\mathbb C^L)$, where $dH$ is Lebesgue measure, $V_{L,a}:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is the chosen potential applied to the real eigenvalues of $H$, and $\mathcal Z_{L,a}:=\int e^{-L\operatorname{tr}V_{L,a}(H)}\,dH$ is finite and positive so that $\mu_{L,a}$ is normalized.

If $\lambda_1(H),\ldots,\lambda_L(H)$ are the eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, the ensemble-averaged eigenvalue-counting measure is $\nu_{L,a}(B):=\int\#\{j:\lambda_j(H)\in B\}\,d\mu_{L,a}(H)$ for each Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$; where it has a density, its leading large-$L$ term is the leading eigenvalue density. A **double-scaling limit** here is a limit along such a family in which $L\to\infty$ and $a\to\infty$, with $a$ the upper endpoint of the leading eigenvalue-density support before shifting, while $V_{L,a}$ is tuned and the energy coordinate is shifted by $E\mapsto E-a$ so that the leading density on the shifted energy region has a finite limit, with $e^{S_0}$ fixed.

In this limit the JT disk density is a smooth leading density, not the discrete spectrum of one finite matrix and not, by itself, a specification of a finite-matrix probability measure. The SSS matrix-integral approach matches the JT genus expansion in this double-scaled framework and is described as a non-unique nonperturbative completion. Therefore the disk density alone specifies neither a unique nonperturbative completion nor the exact energy spectrum of one fixed boundary quantum system (one specified boundary Hilbert space with one specified energy operator, rather than an ensemble of operators). No statement is made about every possible microscopic realization.
items.design_state: Retained the ensemble/nonperturbative-completion warning as a source-backed limitation, without claiming a universal fixed-Hamiltonian interpretation.
